title: Dynamics 365 Contact Center: conversation orchestration with natural language playbooks
summary: The briefing's roadmap dates, administrator prerequisites and publication-based Copilot credit billing are supported. The control path stops before channel selection and publication, and several checklist controls have no corresponding table row; these are minor gaps.

claims.claim: Dynamics 365 Contact Center administrators configure conversation orchestration using natural language playbooks.
claims.quote: Administrators define the logic by using natural-language playbooks, and conversation orchestration handles the execution.

claims.claim: Playbooks act on conversations while they wait in queues.
claims.quote: Conversation waiting in queue | Triggers orchestration while a conversation is waiting in a queue.

claims.claim: A playbook consists of a trigger event plus conditions and actions.
claims.quote: A playbook consists of a trigger event and a set of conditions and actions to run when the trigger event occurs.

claims.claim: Administrators create playbooks from guided templates.
claims.quote: Configure playbooks for each scenario through guided templates that keep instructions focused and reliable.

claims.claim: Dynamic prioritisation is one of the four documented scenario categories.
claims.quote: Dynamic prioritization | Automatically increase or reset conversation priority based on wait time, queue transfers, or queue consults

claims.claim: Overflow handling is a documented playbook scenario.
claims.quote: Overflow handling | Configure real-time overflow actions when queue conditions change

claims.claim: Assignment to a preferred or previously engaged representative is a documented playbook scenario.
claims.quote: Assign to a preferred expert or previously engaged representative | Route conversations to a preferred expert mapped to the contact or to a representative who previously interacted with the customer

claims.claim: Bullseye routing progressively expands eligible representatives through user groups.
claims.quote: Bullseye routing through user groups | Start assignment with a targeted Level 0 user group, then progressively expand to additional user groups as wait time increases.

claims.quote: Transfer to an external number | Transfers the conversation to an external number.

claims.claim: Playbook actions can offer a callback.
claims.quote: Offer callback | Offers the customer a callback as an alternative to continuing to wait in the queue.

claims.claim: Playbook actions can offer voicemail.
claims.quote: Offer voicemail | Offers voicemail as the configured action.

claims.quote: End conversation | Ends the conversation when the configured conditions are met.

claims.claim: Playbook actions can set a representative's presence.
claims.quote: Set user presence | Sets a representative's presence to the specified presence status.

claims.claim: Conversation orchestration is available only for voice and messaging channels.
claims.quote: Conversation orchestration is available for voice and messaging channels only.

claims.claim: The notice and configuration page do not say routing changes for queues without an active playbook.

claims.claim: Context variables such as CustomerTier, Is VIP Customer, Preferred Language, Customer Region and Account Type can shape playbook conditions.

claims.quote: Searched: conversation orchestration language model data processing customer data. Read configure-conversation-orchestration and conversation-orchestration-rai-faq; they describe conversion of playbooks but do not enumerate the model's input payload or processing location.

claims.claim: Customers are responsible for lawful use, including end-user notification and consent where required by applicable laws.
claims.quote: adequately notifying end users that their communications with representatives may be monitored, recorded, or stored and, as required by applicable laws, obtaining consent from end users before using the feature with them.

claims.claim: Published playbooks automatically run configured actions without approval for each runtime execution.
claims.quote: automatically runs the relevant action in accordance with your configured playbooks.

claims.claim: Keeping a conversation unassigned is a supported action.
claims.quote: Keep the conversation unassigned | Keeps the conversation unassigned in its current queue as the configured treatment.

claims.claim: Deleting an active playbook stops conversation orchestration for the corresponding queue immediately.
claims.quote: If you delete an active playbook, conversation orchestration stops for the corresponding queue immediately.

claims.claim: Multiple active playbooks for the same scenario and queue cause a conflict that prevents publication.
claims.quote: You can't have multiple active playbooks for the same scenario and the same queue. This configuration creates a conflict that prevents publishing.

claims.claim: Dynamic prioritisation does not apply to queues with custom prioritisation rules.
claims.quote: It doesn't apply to queues with custom prioritization rules.

claims.where: summary; licensing.notes; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Conversation orchestration consumes Copilot credits at publication rather than runtime, subject to the separately described planned overflow exemption.
claims.quote: Conversation orchestration consumes Copilot credits only when you publish a playbook, which makes the configured orchestration logic active for use.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meter; Why it matters
claims.claim: After publication, a playbook can process any number of customer conversations without additional Copilot credit consumption.
claims.quote: After you publish, the playbook can process any number of customer conversations without consuming extra Copilot credits.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meter; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Saving drafts and enabling conversation orchestration do not consume Copilot credits.
claims.quote: When you save the playbook as a draft or enable conversation orchestration, it doesn't consume Copilot credits.

claims.claim: MC1536059 also states that credits are consumed on publication and not during runtime execution.
claims.quote: Copilot credits are consumed when administrators publish playbooks. The feature does not consume Copilot credits during runtime execution.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meter; Governance controls
claims.claim: Save & publish on an active playbook immediately publishes edits.
claims.quote: For active playbooks: Select Save & publish to save and immediately publish your changes.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meter; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn does not separately state whether Save & publish after an active-playbook edit consumes credits again.
claims.quote: Searched: conversation orchestration Save & publish credits. Read configure-conversation-orchestration and manage-overflow; publication billing and Save & publish are described, but no separate repeat-publication charge statement is given. The expectation is labelled advice to confirm.

claims.claim: Under the planned credit exemption, upgrading a single queue or multiple queues does not use Copilot credits.
claims.quote: Under the planned credit exemption, upgrading a single queue or multiple queues doesn't use Copilot credits.

claims.claim: Playbooks with other conditions, multiple branches or any context variables use Copilot credits.
claims.quote: Playbooks use Copilot credits if they include other conditions, multiple branches, or any context variables. Before you publish these changes, review the publish confirmation. Publishing fails if the required credits aren't available.

claims.quote: For pay-as-you-go, use Microsoft Cost Management in the Azure portal to view detailed usage and adjust spending limits (budgets) to free up more capacity.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Not yet published; rationale: cost

claims.claim: Unified routing must be enabled for the environment.
claims.quote: Unified routing enabled for your environment. At least one queue and workstream is configured for voice or messaging channels. A voice or messaging channel is configured.

claims.claim: Copilot Service admin center > Customer support > Conversation Orchestration > Prompt gallery > scenario category > playbook template > Queues > Edit reaches the playbook queue and channel configuration pane.
claims.quote: go to Customer support > Conversation Orchestration. On the Conversation Orchestration page, select Prompt gallery. In the drop-down field, select a scenario category, and then select a playbook template. Select Queues > Edit to open the queues pane.
claims.fix: Keep the supported path, but complete its note: 'In Queues > Edit, select Channel: Voice or Messaging, then Apply to: All queues, List of queues, or All queues except. Return to the editor, select Save to save a draft, and select Publish to activate the playbook.' The printed route reaches the correct pane but does not itself reach publication.

claims.where: controls[0].api; controls[0].note; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No documented Web API operation provides the equivalent playbook publication control; the documented GET only retrieves records.
claims.quote: Searched: conversation orchestration publish API msdyn_ccuserprompt msdyn_ccplaybookpolicy; msdyn_ccplaybookpolicy publish; msdyn_ccuserprompt msdyn_channel Update. Read configuration, CC User Prompt reference and CC Playbook Policy excerpts; no publication operation is documented.

claims.claim: All controls the governance checklist asks readers to set or review are represented in the controls table.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Set up consumption-based billing'; 'Monitor playbook behaviour with the diagnostics custom query'. Table: 'Which queues and channels a playbook applies to, and whether it is published'.
claims.fix: The billing set-up, administrator-role restriction, custom-prioritisation inventory and diagnostics-monitoring checklist steps lack corresponding control rows. Treat this as a table-coverage gap; do not add rows or unverified paths and automation.

claims.claim: The Save button is disabled for active playbooks.
claims.quote: The Save button is disabled for active playbooks to prevent unintended changes to live routing.

claims.claim: Cancelling an edit reverts the playbook to the last published version.
claims.quote: If you cancel, the playbook reverts to the last published version.

claims.claim: Under the planned exemption, upgraded and newly created playbooks do not use credits when they have one branch containing only the wait-time-in-queue-exceeds condition and no context variables.
claims.quote: Upgraded and newly created playbooks don't use Copilot credits when they have only one branch, that branch contains only the wait time in queue exceeds condition, and they don't use context variables.

claims.claim: Publishing fails if the required Copilot credits are unavailable.
claims.quote: Publishing fails if the required credits aren't available.

claims.claim: For the selected voice or messaging channel, queue scope can be All queues, List of queues or All queues except.
claims.quote: All queues: Applies to all queues for the selected channel. List of queues: Select specific queues from the list. All queues except: Applies to all queues except the ones you exclude.

claims.claim: Saving a draft does not activate the playbook.
claims.quote: Draft | The playbook is saved but not active. You can make changes freely.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents moving playbooks between environments by adding CC User Prompt to a solution and exporting and importing the solution.
claims.quote: Move a playbook from a source environment to a destination environment by adding it to a solution and using the solution export and import. Select and add CC User Prompt from other tables to the solution.

claims.claim: The queues and context variables a playbook references must already exist in the destination before importing it.
claims.quote: A playbook references other configuration tables, like queues and context variables. Every related entity a playbook uses must already exist in the destination environment or organization before you import the solution, otherwise, the solution import fails.

claims.quote: RetrieveMultiple Event: True | GET /msdyn_ccuserprompts See Query data

claims.quote: RetrieveMultiple Event: True | GET /msdyn_ccuserprompts See Query data

claims.claim: The configuration page names CC User Prompt in its solution-migration instructions, not as a Web API publication operation.
claims.quote: Export the solution from the source environment: Select and add CC User Prompt from other tables to the solution.
